A colossal arched stained-glass window pours shafts of crimson and violet light across the towering stacks, dust motes drifting in the beams.
A great brass orrery turns slowly overhead, its gilded planets casting long moving shadows across every gallery and reading alcove below.
A forbidden vault-door looms deep in the stacks, its surface covered in warding runes that glow faintly red against the dark stone.
A glowing knowledge-orb hovers above a central pedestal, pulsing with soft golden light, ringed by the library's tallest and oldest shelves.
A vast central staircase spirals upward through every tier of the library, its carved stone banister worn smooth by countless scholarly hands.
A great reading-table sprawls at the library's heart, strewn with unfurled maps, celestial charts, and ink-stained manuscripts weighted open with brass.
An ancient statue of a robed sage stands at the hall's center, one stone hand raised, the other clutching a worn open book.
A glowing portal-mirror dominates one wall, its silver surface rippling gently, reflecting not the room behind the viewer but somewhere else entirely.
A still pool fills the library's center, its dark water perfectly reflecting the painted ceiling vault high above in every exact detail.
A towering central pillar rises floor to ceiling, every surface carved with dense lore in spiraling script no living scholar can fully read.
A hovering glowing tome rests open above a stone altar, its pages turning slowly on their own, luminous text shifting with each turn.
A great clockwork astrolabe fills the domed apex, its brass rings clicking through alignments, tracking stars whose positions correspond to no known sky.
A tremendous iron chandelier hung with hundreds of self-lighting candles descends from the vault, its warm glow reaching the deepest shadowed reading corners.
A collapsed section of ceiling has let in a shaft of open sky, through which climbing vines now curl between the highest shelves.
A cracked hourglass taller than three men stands on a marble dais, its frozen sand somehow still suspended mid-fall inside the broken glass.
A great bronze lectern shaped like a rearing dragon holds an enormous open atlas, its spread wings forming the angled surface for the book.
A long gallery of locked iron cages lines one wall, each containing a single chained manuscript deemed too dangerous for ordinary scholarly handling.
A softly humming crystal column rises from the floor, facets refracting library candlelight into slow-wheeling constellations that drift across the surrounding shelving.
A carved stone archway at the hall's far end frames pure darkness, from which a faint warm wind carries the smell of old pages.
A great mechanical librarian automaton stands dormant at the catalog desk, brass fingers still resting on an index, waiting for the word to wake.
An enormous celestial globe dominates a side chamber, hand-painted with continents that match no current world map and annotated in a dead tongue.
A sunken amphitheater at the library's heart holds rings of tiered stone seats facing a raised speaking plinth still marked with old chalk diagrams.
A wall of sealed glass cases displays open grimoires under preservation wards, their pages still slowly rewriting themselves even behind the enchanted glass.
A narrow bridge of pale stone arcs between two upper gallery tiers high above the floor, lined with the most restricted shelf of all.
A massive armillary sphere of tarnished silver sits in the entrance rotunda, arrow-thin rings tilted at every angle, a compass for no ordinary journey.
